That's a good question. An early beta user asked me that same question (although he had a fixed number of columns and just needed the user to specify rows).

I have put together a package called shiny-incubator for Shiny components that might be of general interest, but aren't ready or aren't suitable for inclusion in the core Shiny package. You can install it easily if you have Hadley's devtools package installed (and if not, you can install devtools from CRAN).

library(devtools)

I have not had time to polish it up and don't have time right at the moment, but it should give you an idea of what's possible. (If there are any intrepid JavaScript hackers out there who want to finish the job, that would be hugely helpful!)

messages.subject: Re: tutorial examples not working with internet explorer 9 as default browser.
messages.subject_clean: tutorial examples not working with internet explorer 9 as default browser.
messages.body_plain:
Sorry, I think we forgot to document this--we have serious compatibility issues with IE9 and below. That's a pretty big oversight, we'll try to correct that soon.
IE8 currently doesn't work with either Shiny running locally, or Shiny server (e.g. our live example apps on the Shiny homepages).
IE9 currently doesn't work with Shiny running locally, but it does work with Shiny server.
IE10 should work fine with both versions of Shiny.
If you can install Chrome Frame <http://www.google.com/chromeframe> for IE (any supported version), then both versions of Shiny will work.
Please let us know if this is a problem for you, including what version of IE you need support for, and whether it's an option for your users to install a more up-to-date browser. If IE compatibility is really going to stop adoption of Shiny in companies then we would consider tackling the quite significant engineering tasks needed to solve these compatibility issues. But of course that means time we couldn't spend improving the rest of the framework. So we definitely need your feedback to help us prioritize.

(In case you are interested in the technical details, Shiny relies heavily on a feature of HTML5 called Websockets. IE8 and 9 don't support websockets; Microsoft used to have a free plugin for IE9 that enabled websocket support, but they seem to have pulled it down since IE10 was released. Shiny server works around this limitation by using communication platforms from other languages (that isn't available in R) that it translates to/from websocket traffic. That's why IE9 works on Shiny server but not locally. IE8 doesn't even work on Shiny server because of a different, unrelated issue <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3586749/how-to-get-around-ie8-32k-limit-on-datauri-on-base64-encode>.)

Thanks for the question!

messages.subject: Re: Product Roadmap
messages.body_plain:
> Is there a plan to add validation for user input fields client side i.e. a input field should be a number or string, etc

Sure, that seems like a really good candidate for our next release.

> How are server side errors propagated to the user/UI - for example, if you user requests invalid date range or the data doesn't exist, how would you display that information gracefully to the UI

The easiest way right now is to simply use R's default error handling, e.g. stop("Invalid date range"). When these errors make it all the way to an output without being caught, they are displayed in place of the output. The default style is for the error to appear in red, prepended with the word "Error:" in bold, but that is all customizable using CSS.

> Are there plans to add authentication support i.e. users, groups, permissions per view, etc (something similar to the django admin module which comes for free out of the box)

Definitely user authentication. I don't know what granularity at which the permissions will apply. If you could describe the scenario you have in mind for django-like permissions, it would be hugely helpful. (You're welcome to e-mail me off-list if you don't want to publicize details of your app.)

> Would there be support for automatically updating the UI without any user input e.g. push updates to the data to the user.

Yes, we have not written up examples of this yet but the pieces are there.

The most common way that changes ripple through the system is through users touching inputs, but another way that we already support is time-based invalidation. Here's an example I just wrote that has two different components that are varying over time:

Demo: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/jcheng/time/
Source: https://gist.github.com/4044364

This might not be intuitive yet if you're still getting your head around reactive programming, but the point is that the "invalidateLater" function is all that is needed to build, say, a reactiveFileInput function that pushes changed values through the system. An intrepid Shiny user could build such a function now, but if you wait until the next release we can probably save you the trouble.

> Are there any limitations in using existing R packages like ggplot2/googleVis/ or tikz images

No problem with ggplot2, and in general visualizations that write to R's default graphics device should work fine. googleVis will need some customization to work with Shiny, similar to the kind of stuff Markus had to do to get googleVis to work with R Markdown. I'm not familiar with tikz.

> How would you stitch together more complicated applications - for example, if you expand on your stocks example and add another view which shows fundamental time-series data, how would the navigation work.

Currently Shiny is focused on single-page apps, so you'd need to integrate all the views into a single page. Tabs actually work pretty nicely for that in a lot of cases: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/mosaic/CIgeometry/

> How would you add static data to pages

Can you be more specific about "static data"?

> What other widgets are you guys planning on adding

We don't have anything specific planned right now, we're just waiting to see what people request.

I'll add that we are more excited about helping folks in the community to design and package their own widgets that can be easily used by all Shiny users.

Thanks for the great questions--hope that helps!

messages.subject_clean: How to Integrate shiny with rApache?
messages.body_plain:
Unfortunately, no.

Shiny represents a new class of web applications that require very little HTTP and a lot of websockets. Whereas traditional web applications, including those hosted on rApache  and Rook, rely on the URL namespace for application logic, location of assets, etc... Shiny applications and those like them house their logic in javascript MVC patterns and communicate solely over websockets.

Shiny apps are hosted using the R websockets package which acts more like a tcp server than a web server, and that architecture just doesn't fit with rApache, or even apache for that matter.

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: button that's not a submitButton
messages.body_plain:
If you do <button type="button"></button> (or in R, tags$button(type="button", ...) ) then it won't freeze the UI. Only <button type="submit"></button> (which I believe is the default if you don't specify the type) will freeze the UI. Adapting the incrementing button example should work; as long as the input is updated with a distinct value every time the button is clicked, then the reactive stuff on the server will react.

I think I forgot to document something that will come in handy as you try to do this. You can run "options(shiny.trace=TRUE)" before calling runApp, and your R console will show messages going from the browser to the server and vice versa. In this way you can easily see if clicking on the button actually causes anything to get sent.

Let me know how it goes!

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to change the properties of some UI control.

For instance, say I have a selectInput that lets me select different datasets, which are time series over a certain number of days.
I then create a slider that lets me choose a range of days to display:

sliderInput("daysRange", "Range of days", min=1, max=10, value=c(1, 10))

Now, the datasets do not necessarily have 10 days, so I would like to change max when I change the dataframe, so that if I load a 30 days time series the slider will update to have max equal to 30.

How can I do that?

>
> (In case you are interested in the technical details, Shiny relies heavily on a feature of HTML5 called Websockets. IE8 and 9 don't support websockets; Microsoft used to have a free plugin for IE9 that enabled websocket support, but they seem to have pulled it down since IE10 was released. Shiny server works around this limitation by using communication platforms from other languages (that isn't available in R) that it translates to/from websocket traffic. messages.body_plain: Yes, there are a number of options. The first thing to know is that all of the calls we use in ui.R/shinyUI are just HTML generating functions. For example, if you type this at the R console: > textInput('foo', 'Foo') [1] "\n" attr(,"html") [1] TRUE You can see that the textInput function doesn't do anything magical, it just outputs HTML. You can output HTML yourself in a number of ways. 1) You can write your HTML as a string and wrap it in a call to the HTML function. 2) You can use the tag generating functions that Shiny comes with. 3) You can put your HTML in a separate file, and include it. I've included examples of all 3 in this gist: https://gist.github.com/4052973 You can run it with runGist('https://gist.github.com/4052973'). If you have other assets--CSS, images, JavaScript files--that you want to include in your application, you can create a www directory inside of your Shiny app directory. Any files you put in there will be available to your page. You should refer to them with relative URLs. For example, if you had www/logo.png, you would do HTML('') or img(src="logo.png"). If anything about that is unclear please let me know. As for the auth stuff, that sounds very much like what we have in mind. So far I don't think anything you've mentioned sounds out of scope for us. Thanks for the valuable feedback!

I was having problems in the following application with 2 sliders:

messages.subject: Re: Dynamic plot width/height
messages.body_plain:
The default setting is to scale with window width (actually to be precise, with the size of the plot container's width). Scaling height-wise in generally tricky in HTML, Shiny can autoscale height with container height but won't assist you with making the container vertically scale. You could use CSS to absolutely position the div container and then make sure you pass height=100% to the plotOutput call.

If you can't figure it out let me know and I'll cobble up a simple example.

messages.subject: Re: Persistent data?
messages.body_plain:
Just define a reactive function that loads data from your file input:

myData <- reactive(function() {
  read.csv(input$file[1]$datapath)
})

Then from inside your outputs, call myData() to retrieve the data. Don't worry about read.csv being called multiple times; the function behind myData will only execute when input$file changes, no matter how many times myData is referred to.

messages.body_plain:
Apologies for dropping in late on this, but from what I understand about sockjs is that it will use the most efficient transport based on the browser. Thus, websockets are chosen for modern browsers and apache won't ever be able to proxy those requests.

I'm speculating here, but one possible solution could have RStudio's Shiny server detect that a client is requesting an app through a proxy (by inspecting certain HTTP headers?) and have the sockjs engine downgrade the transport to the lowest common denominator.

2012. november 9., péntek 1:33:07 UTC+1 időpontban Joe Cheng [RStudio] a következőt írta:
> Sorry, I think we forgot to document this--we have serious compatibility issues with IE9 and below. That's a pretty big oversight, we'll try to correct that soon.
> IE8 currently doesn't work with either Shiny running locally, or Shiny server (e.g. our live example apps on the Shiny homepages).
> IE9 currently doesn't work with Shiny running locally, but it does work with Shiny server.
> IE10 should work fine with both versions of Shiny.
> If you can install Chrome Frame <http://www.google.com/chromeframe> for IE (any supported version), then both versions of Shiny will work.
> Please let us know if this is a problem for you, including what version of IE you need support for, and whether it's an option for your users to install a more up-to-date browser. If IE compatibility is really going to stop adoption of Shiny in companies then we would consider tackling the quite significant engineering tasks needed to solve these compatibility issues. But of course that means time we couldn't spend improving the rest of the framework. So we definitely need your feedback to help us prioritize.
>
> (In case you are interested in the technical details, Shiny relies heavily on a feature of HTML5 called Websockets. IE8 and 9 don't support websockets; Microsoft used to have a free plugin for IE9 that enabled websocket support, but they seem to have pulled it down since IE10 was released. Shiny server works around this limitation by using communication platforms from other languages (that isn't available in R) that it translates to/from websocket traffic. That's why IE9 works on Shiny server but not locally. IE8 doesn't even work on Shiny server because of a different, unrelated issue <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3586749/how-to-get-around-ie8-32k-limit-on-datauri-on-base64-encode>.)
>
> Thanks for the question!

messages.subject: Re: Pushing app to Shiny hosting account
messages.subject_clean: Pushing app to Shiny hosting account
messages.body_plain:
Sorry, I just realized from the previous thread that you're on Mac.

The easiest point-and-click way is to download an app like Cyberduck <http://cyberduck.ch/> and configure it for SFTP access using the credentials I gave you. Once you connect, you'll be looking at your home directory on glimmer.rstudio.com <http://glimmer.rstudio.com>. Use Cyberduck to create a new folder called ShinyApps. Now drag any Shiny application directories from your local Finder window right onto Cyberduck and that should upload them. The goal is to have e.g. ~/ShinyApps/myapp/server.R and ~/ShinyApps/myapp/ui.R.

Simply the presence of those app directories in the ~/ShinyApps directory will make them available on http://glimmer.rstudio.com/awegro/<whatever>.

If you prefer command line, you can use:

rsync -avz --delete <path-to-local-app-directory> awe...@glimmer.rstudio.com:~/ShinyApps/
Important: Make sure that your path-to-local-app-directory does NOT include a trailing slash.

If you get tired of typing your password every time you can set up ssh authentication <http://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/help/jpmg/ssh/authorized_keys_howto.html>.

Let me know if that is enough...

messages.subject: Re: Apache proxying
messages.body_plain:
Ah, that seems to work. FWIW, this is the steps I used:
Spin up a basic 64-bit Amazon Linux AMI. Log in via ssh.
Do "yum install R R-devel" to get R and the ability to build packages.
Start R. Install the shiny package via the instructions in the beta email. Also install other packages needed.
In the AWS console, set up a security group that allows connections to 8100 from your.ip.address/31. I had to fiddle with this a few times until it seemed to take.
>From R, library(shiny); runExample("01_hello") should work
Install your server.R and ui.R (and if needed other files).
R -e "shiny::runApp('.')"
With a free micro instance, it all works, but those VMs are not fast. Easily 4 or 5 times slower than my MacBook Air.

 -Harlan

messages.subject: The path collected by fileInput
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have tried to follow the example use of fileInput in this example [1] to attempt to open a local sqlite database (using Chrome).  It seems that after selecting a file with the fileInput widget, the full path of the selected file is not stored.  Instead, only the name of the file is stored.  The evidence for this is that I the following error message after selecting "test.db" from the browser UI:

> runApp("/Users/arq5x/shiny/")

Listening on port 8100
     name     size type
1 test.db 16048128
                                                                                 datapath
1 /var/folders/7r/c3r2sn4j3dvg4c62jr1dq8_w0000gn/T//RtmpAk41Pt/e23a2c42561fcb0d044d05f5/0
Error in path.expand(dbname) : invalid 'path' argument
Error in path.expand(dbname) : invalid 'path' argument

Am I missing something obvious?  I know the server code can work since it works fine when I hard-code a full path to a file in the dbConnect statement instead of using input$db

Code below:

ui.R
===
library(shiny)

# Define UI for dataset viewer application
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  headerPanel("Gemini"),

  sidebarPanel(

    fileInput("db", "gemini database", multiple=FALSE),
    checkboxInput("lof", "Loss of function")
  ),

  mainPanel(
    tableOutput("view")
  )
))

server.R
=======
library(shiny)
library(RSQLite)
# Define server logic required to summarize and view the selected dataset
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
    output$view <- reactiveTable(function() {
        if (! is.null(input$db)) {
            print(input$db)
            con <- dbConnect(dbDriver("SQLite"),
                         dbname = input$db)
            query = paste("select ", "chrom, start, end",
                          " from variants limit 10")
            df = dbGetQuery(con, query)
            df
        }
    })
})

[1] https://gist.github.com/4050398

messages.body_plain:
Are you looking to allow the user to browse the server's entire filesystem? Or are we just talking about one folder? If the latter, then you could consider using a selectInput with list.files populating the choices (and verify, when you're reading the choice, that it's definitely a file in the directory you expect and not malicious input with ../../ etc.). If the former, there are ways I could think of enabling this but you'd really need to think through the security implications of exposing your server's filesystem.

If this is only for local use then putting a call to file.choose() behind a button is probably the way to go. Someone on this forum submitted a code sample for an action button, I'll see if I can get it or something similar in shiny-incubator.

messages.subject: Re: Force size of 'device window'
messages.body_plain:
On the plotOutput function, you can specify dimensions in CSS format (e.g. "200px" for 200 pixels, "75%" for 75% of the available space). So it's easy to make a fixed-size plot (or just fix the height and let the width go to 100%, which is the default behavior). However, it sounds like you might be asking for a scaling image that keeps a particular aspect ratio (or even a min/max aspect ratio)--that's not currently possible (without JavaScript), though a great idea.

messages.subject: reactiveTable - passing arguments to xtable vs. print.xtable
messages.subject_clean: reactiveTable - passing arguments to xtable vs. print.xtable
messages.body_plain:
The documentation for reactiveTable(fun,...) passes any arguments besides the function to xtable; however, the xtable() function itself ignores additional arguments that are supported by print.xtable() like include.rownames. So you instead have to set global options like this:

  output$table <- reactiveTable(function() {
    options(xtable.include.rownames=FALSE)
    data.frame(x=data())
  })

Is there any particular reason to call just xtable and not print.xtable() which supports tons of options for customizing the output.

Thanks

-Haider

messages.subject: Need for more graphical control and upload/download
messages.subject_clean: Need for more graphical control and upload/download
messages.body_plain:
Just set Shiny up on my pharmacogenomics group's R-studio server here at Mayo clinic. Love it. I've set it up to generate fairly detailed reactive plots for any genes of interest, and am curious to see how well those with less computational expertise take to it.

Two initial comments though:

1. It would be good to have more control over graphics dimensions. I see this has already come up in another posting. I feel more can be done. When running Shiny on data like mine (tens of thousands of genes) a plot for any gene may have 1 feature or it may have 50 features. It all depends on the amount of data for the gene. Normally I have my output dimensions be some multiple of feature number (e.g. height=feature_number*100). There doesn't seem to be a fuss-free way to do this in Shiny. There also doesn't seem to be a fuss-free way of controlling the ability to scroll images.

2. I see Shiny being really useful in groups like mine where there is far too much data and team members want a way to visualise a lot and then trim down to easily manageable data for their own analysis. Allowing me to get on with my own research without many low-level requests! It would be good to have an upload and download feature. Where standardised data formats can be uploaded, merged with the greater set of data, analysis run and results returned. Also any results from the reactive plot exploration downloaded (e.g. CSV of top features for a gene).

Great work so far,
Quin
P.S. Please keep the production quality server version free, and focus on charging for a hosting and support service!

Can you tell me what doesn't work about file.choose from a button? I just added an action button into the shiny-incubator package (use library(devtools); install_github('shiny-incubator', 'rstudio') to install) and it seemed to work fine with file.choose for me.

Two things to note: If you cancel out of file.choose, it raises an error; if that's not the behavior you want then you can do result <- try(file.choose()) and then use is(result, 'try-error') to see if the user cancelled or not.

Secondly, if you don't want the file.choose to appear right away, but only when the button is clicked, you can check if the button value is 0 and don't do anything in that case.

messages.subject: Re: Need for more graphical control and upload/download
messages.subject_clean: Need for more graphical control and upload/download
messages.body_plain:
>
> 1. It would be good to have more control over graphics dimensions. I see this has already come up in another posting. I feel more can be done. When running Shiny on data like mine (tens of thousands of genes) a plot for any gene may have 1 feature or it may have 50 features. It all depends on the amount of data for the gene. Normally I have my output dimensions be some multiple of feature number (e.g. height=feature_number*100). There doesn't seem to be a fuss-free way to do this in Shiny. There also doesn't seem to be a fuss-free way of controlling the ability to scroll images.

Good suggestion--I'm about to check in a change that lets you use a function to specify the width and/or height. The function can refer to reactive inputs and functions. This way if you have your data subset saved as a reactive function, you can define the width/height in terms of that data and it will automatically resize/redraw the graph.

I'm not sure what the right answer is for scrolling right now. I was tempted to add a generic scrollPanel but I don't think it makes that much sense in light of the way our current "template" (pageWithSidebar) works--I think we need a template that is more app-like and less page-like.

>
> 2. I see Shiny being really useful in groups like mine where there is far too much data and team members want a way to visualise a lot and then trim down to easily manageable data for their own analysis. Allowing me to get on with my own research without many low-level requests! It would be good to have an upload and download feature. Where standardised data formats can be uploaded, merged with the greater set of data, analysis run and results returned. Also any results from the reactive plot exploration downloaded (e.g. CSV of top features for a gene).

There is a sort of half-baked input feature which is fileInput. The main limitations are that it only works with very recent versions of Chrome, Safari, and Firefox, and it doesn't show progress. But it should mostly work. I'm working on the download feature, most of the plumbing is done but I'm still working on what the functions should look like.

>
> P.S. Please keep the production quality server version free, and focus on charging for a hosting and support service!

The feedback we've heard so far is that corporations mostly want server software, and it's mostly individuals and people in academia who want the hosting service. We're thinking hard about our business model, stay tuned...

ocbcDriverConnect(connection = "Driver=SQL Server; Server=TESTSERVER;Integrated Security=SSPI;Database=TESTDB")

messages.subject: Re: Need for more graphical control and upload/download
messages.subject_clean: Need for more graphical control and upload/download
messages.body_plain:
Great to hear, Joe. I look forward to seeing the progress. I demo'ed my Shiny genomics app to the team today and it was extremely well received.

I think you may be surprised about what people want. I've hosted my own commercial analysis software (all R/S+ back end). 5 years ago everybody wanted to bring servers in-house for security reasons but software as service is pretty standard these days... if you can assure basic data protection. For my company tying in R analysis web services with flexible e-commerce features was also key for customer-facing applications. I'm sure given enough time all these good things will come to Shiny ;)

Good luck!
Quin

_______________________________________________

find me at http://uk.linkedin.com/pub/quin-wills/42/116/600
_______________________________________________

On 19 November 2012 17:12, Joe Cheng <j...@joecheng.com> wrote:

>
> >
> > 1. It would be good to have more control over graphics dimensions. I see this has already come up in another posting. I feel more can be done. When running Shiny on data like mine (tens of thousands of genes) a plot for any gene may have 1 feature or it may have 50 features. It all depends on the amount of data for the gene. Normally I have my output dimensions be some multiple of feature number (e.g. height=feature_number*100). There doesn't seem to be a fuss-free way to do this in Shiny. There also doesn't seem to be a fuss-free way of controlling the ability to scroll images.
>
> Good suggestion--I'm about to check in a change that lets you use a function to specify the width and/or height. The function can refer to reactive inputs and functions. This way if you have your data subset saved as a reactive function, you can define the width/height in terms of that data and it will automatically resize/redraw the graph.
>
> I'm not sure what the right answer is for scrolling right now. I was tempted to add a generic scrollPanel but I don't think it makes that much sense in light of the way our current "template" (pageWithSidebar) works--I think we need a template that is more app-like and less page-like.
>
> >
> > 2. I see Shiny being really useful in groups like mine where there is far too much data and team members want a way to visualise a lot and then trim down to easily manageable data for their own analysis. Allowing me to get on with my own research without many low-level requests! It would be good to have an upload and download feature. Where standardised data formats can be uploaded, merged with the greater set of data, analysis run and results returned. Also any results from the reactive plot exploration downloaded (e.g. CSV of top features for a gene).
>
> There is a sort of half-baked input feature which is fileInput. The main limitations are that it only works with very recent versions of Chrome, Safari, and Firefox, and it doesn't show progress. But it should mostly work. I'm working on the download feature, most of the plumbing is done but I'm still working on what the functions should look like.
>
> >
> > P.S. Please keep the production quality server version free, and focus on charging for a hosting and support service!
>
> The feedback we've heard so far is that corporations mostly want server software, and it's mostly individuals and people in academia who want the hosting service. We're thinking hard about our business model, stay tuned...

> --
>
>

messages.subject: Conditional Tab Panels
messages.body_plain:
Hi, may I suggest to allow conditionally showing/hiding tab panels (similarly to conditionalPanel)?
An option would be to insert a line into the tabsetPanel function:
if(!is.null(divTag$attribs$condition)) liTag$attribs$`data-display-if` <- divTag$attribs$condition
and then e.g.
tabPanel("Table", tableOutput("table"),condition="input.dist=='norm'")
Example here: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/szakacs/test6/
However, in this case the shiny.js should be modified to activate another tab if needed.
Thanks

> >
> > I'm speculating here, but one possible solution could have RStudio's Shiny server detect that a client is requesting an app through a proxy (by inspecting certain HTTP headers?) and have the sockjs engine downgrade the transport to the lowest common denominator.

> > > Thanks for your patience.

> > >

messages.subject: Re: Need for more graphical control and upload/download
messages.subject_clean: Need for more graphical control and upload/download
messages.body_plain:
Normally to get the very latest changes from GitHub you would need to have the devtools package installed and do devtools::install_github('shiny', 'rstudio')

But in this particular case I just happened to rev the Shiny package yesterday so you can follow the normal instructions for installing the package on http://rstudio.com/shiny.

On Mon, Nov 19, 2012 at 9:32 PM, Andrew Elliott <awe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Great - I think that this will solve my height issue too. Do I just need to update the library or is there another function I need to use?

>
> On Monday, November 19, 2012 3:12:43 PM UTC-8, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> >
> > >
> > > 1. It would be good to have more control over graphics dimensions. I see this has already come up in another posting. I feel more can be done. When running Shiny on data like mine (tens of thousands of genes) a plot for any gene may have 1 feature or it may have 50 features. It all depends on the amount of data for the gene. Normally I have my output dimensions be some multiple of feature number (e.g. height=feature_number*100). There doesn't seem to be a fuss-free way to do this in Shiny. There also doesn't seem to be a fuss-free way of controlling the ability to scroll images.
> >
> > Good suggestion--I'm about to check in a change that lets you use a function to specify the width and/or height. The function can refer to reactive inputs and functions. This way if you have your data subset saved as a reactive function, you can define the width/height in terms of that data and it will automatically resize/redraw the graph.
> >
> > I'm not sure what the right answer is for scrolling right now. I was tempted to add a generic scrollPanel but I don't think it makes that much sense in light of the way our current "template" (pageWithSidebar) works--I think we need a template that is more app-like and less page-like.
> >
> > >
> > > 2. I see Shiny being really useful in groups like mine where there is far too much data and team members want a way to visualise a lot and then trim down to easily manageable data for their own analysis. Allowing me to get on with my own research without many low-level requests! It would be good to have an upload and download feature. Where standardised data formats can be uploaded, merged with the greater set of data, analysis run and results returned. Also any results from the reactive plot exploration downloaded (e.g. CSV of top features for a gene).
> >
> > There is a sort of half-baked input feature which is fileInput. The main limitations are that it only works with very recent versions of Chrome, Safari, and Firefox, and it doesn't show progress. But it should mostly work. I'm working on the download feature, most of the plumbing is done but I'm still working on what the functions should look like.
> >
> > >
> > > P.S. Please keep the production quality server version free, and focus on charging for a hosting and support service!
> >
> > The feedback we've heard so far is that corporations mostly want server software, and it's mostly individuals and people in academia who want the hosting service. We're thinking hard about our business model, stay tuned...
>

> --
>
>

I think there's a lot more we need to get this working. It looks like RODBC provides the connection from R to ODBC in general, but ODBC is just a general protocol for talking to databases--you need an ODBC driver for MS SQL. On Linux it looks like the free one is called FreeTDS, so I've installed that on glimmer. However it looks like you also need to configure FreeTDS to know about your server in /etc/freetds/freetds.conf... which we can do, I guess... it's just weird as this is a global config file that needs to be edited by the administrator every time. I don't know if we'd offer this as part of our hosting service but I'm definitely interested to see how we can get this to work for future reference.

messages.body_plain:
Hi

Just signed up to the Shiny Server beta. I tried to install the package RPostgreSQL to connect to my postgresql database, but unfortunately if fails the basic sanity test (which I think checks to see if PostgreSQL is installed on the Ubuntu host. This is the error message in RStudio Server

In file included from RS-PQescape.c:7:0:
RS-PostgreSQL.h:23:26: fatal error: libpq-fe.h: No such file or directory
compilation terminated.
make: *** [RS-PQescape.o] Error 1
ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘RPostgreSQL’
* removing ‘/home/onsideanalysis/R/library/RPostgreSQL’
Warning in install.packages :
  installation of package ‘RPostgreSQL’ had non-zero exit status

I tried then doing a local install of postgresql which seems to work well, and then building RPostgreSQL against this local install. I seemed to get further (everything seemed to compile) but when the package tested if it could be loaded it failed again

installing to /home/onsideanalysis/R/library/RPostgreSQL/libs
** R
** inst
** preparing package for lazy loading
Creating a generic function for ‘format’ from package ‘base’ in package ‘RPostgreSQL’
Creating a generic function for ‘print’ from package ‘base’ in package ‘RPostgreSQL’
** help
*** installing help indices
** building package indices
** installing vignettes
** testing if installed package can be loaded
Error in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...) :
  unable to load shared object '/home/onsideanalysis/R/library/RPostgreSQL/libs/RPostgreSQL.so':
  libpq.so.5: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
Error: loading failed
Execution halted
ERROR: loading failed
* removing ‘/home/onsideanalysis/R/library/RPostgreSQL’
Warning in install.packages :
  installation of package ‘RPostgreSQL’ had non-zero exit status

Is there any chance postgresql could be installed on the host machine to avoid having to compile against local. I'm pretty sure that would fix it.

Many thanks
Dave

Dear all,
I am trying to write a very simple shiny program in which I select a column of a data.frame called "datos" (defined with a sidebarPanel in the ui.r), then
1. plot the boxplot of the selected column (called "variable" in the ui.r)
and
2. show the summary of the selected column

shinyServer(function(input,output){

#first define formulaText:

formulaText <- reactive(function(){

  paste(input$variable,"~datos$R")

                                   })

#then define the field gPlot for output:

output$gPlot <- reactivePlot(function(){

   plot.new <http://plot.new>() #

   boxplot(as.formula(formulaText()),

           data = mpgData

           )

                                         })

So far so good. But how can I do to define also an output$summary with the summary(input$variable)?

Do I need to define something like formulaText **before** then pass it to the output$summary?

A more general question is: how do variables from input and fields of output communicate to each other?

Why I can not simply write something like the following structure?

output$summary <- reactivePrint(function() {

    summary(input$variable)

    })

Many thanks,

Giovanna

messages.subject: Passing lists around
messages.body_plain:
I deployed my first shiny app on glimmer today (http://glimmer.rstudio.com/rpruim/SamplingDists/).  In the process I had to implement two work-arounds for things that didn't work the way I first tried.  Both issues involve passing lists around between ui.R and server.R.

Thanks in advance for any tips/suggestions.

Issue 1: Using selectInput() to set a list of things.

My app allows users to select a population distribution.  I wanted input$popDist to contain a named list with slots for rdist, distName, and params, but I couldn't seem to get it working.It is currently implemented in ui.R:

 selectInput("popDist", "Population",
                list("Normal" = "normal",
                     "Beta" = "beta",
                     "Gamma" = "gamma",
                     "Weibull" = "weibull"  )
                ),   # end selectInput

and server.R:

   params <- reactive( function() {
switch(popDist(),
  "normal" = list(mean=input$mean, sd=input$sd),
  "beta" = list(shape1=input$shape1, shape2=input$shape2),
  "gamma" = list(shape=input$shape, scale=input$scale),
  "weibull" = list(shape=input$shape, scale=input$scale)
  )} )

rdist <- reactive( function() {
switch(popDist(),
  "normal" = "rnorm",
  "beta" = "rbeta",
  "gamma" = "rgamma",
  "weibull" = "rweibull"
  )} )

distName <- reactive( function() {
switch(popDist(),
  "normal" = "norm",
  "beta" = "beta",
  "gamma" = "gamma",
  "weibull" = "weibull"
  )} )

Is there a better way to do this?

Issue 2:  Grouping results from multiple controls into a list

The different distributions have different parameters, so I used conditionalPanel() to show controls only for appropriate parameters.  Easy enough.  But I really wanted the results of the multiple sliders in one conditionalPanel() to be returned as a list rather than as individual slots in input.  Again, there is a work-around (see below), but I would have liked something tidier.

in ui.R:
conditionalPanel(
condition = "input.popDist == 'beta'",
sliderInput("shape1", "shape1: ", min=0.1, max=10, value=1, step=0.05),
sliderInput("shape2", "shape2: ", min=0.1, max=10, value=1, step=0.05)
),
conditionalPanel(
condition = "input.popDist == 'gamma'",
sliderInput("shape", "shape: ", min=0.1, max=10, value=1, step=0.05),
sliderInput("scale", "scale: ", min=0.1, max=10, value=1, step=0.05)
),
conditionalPanel(
condition = "input.popDist == 'weibull'",
sliderInput("shape", "shape: ", min=0.1, max=10, value=1, step=0.05),
sliderInput("scale", "scale: ", min=0.1, max=10, value=1, step=0.05)
),
conditionalPanel(
condition = "input.popDist == 'normal'",
sliderInput("mean", "mean: ", min=0, max=400, value=0),
sliderInput("sd", "st. dev.: ", min=0.1, max=20, value=1, step=.1)
)

in server.R:

    params <- reactive( function() {
switch(popDist(),
  "normal" = list(mean=input$mean, sd=input$sd),
  "beta" = list(shape1=input$shape1, shape2=input$shape2),
  "gamma" = list(shape=input$shape, scale=input$scale),
  "weibull" = list(shape=input$shape, scale=input$scale)
  )} )

cheers

messages.subject: Re: Passing lists around
messages.body_plain:
Hi Randall,

I think the best thing would be to have some objects in your global namespace that define the characteristics of normal, beta, gamma, and weibull. You can define these objects in a global.R file, and it will be automatically read at app startup and those objects will be visible in ui.R and server.R.

Here's a gist in case the code I paste below gets mangled:
https://gist.github.com/4136824

# global.R

dists <- list(

  normal = list(

    label = "Normal",

    func = rnorm,

    inputs = tagList(

      sliderInput("mean", "mean: ", min=0, max=400, value=0),

      sliderInput("sd", "st. dev.: ", min=0.1, max=20, value=1, step=.1)

    ),

    params = c("mean", "sd")

  ),

  beta = list(

    label = "Beta",

    func = rbeta,

    inputs = tagList(

      sliderInput("shape1", "shape1: ", min=0.1, max=10, value=1, step=0.05),

      sliderInput("shape2", "shape2: ", min=0.1, max=10, value=1, step=0.05)

    ),

    params = c("shape1", "shape2")

  )

)
distChoices <- names(dists)

names(distChoices) <- sapply(dists, function(x) {x$label})

# ui.R

selectInput("popDist", "Population", distChoices),

lapply(names(dists), function(name) {

  conditionalPanel(condition = sprintf("input.popDist == '%s'", name),

                   dists[[name]]$inputs)

})

# server.R

params <- reactive(function() {

  values <- lapply(dists[[input$popDist]]$params, function(param) {

    input[param]

  })

  names(values) <- dists[[input$popDist]]$params

  values

})
rdist <- reactive(function() {

  dists[[input$popDist]]$func

})

> My app allows users to select a population distribution.  I wanted input$popDist to contain a named list with slots for rdist, distName, and params, but I couldn't seem to get it working.It is currently implemented in ui.R:

> and server.R:

> switch(popDist(),

>   "gamma" = list(shape=input$shape, scale=input$scale),

messages.subject: Re: passing arguments to xtable
messages.body_plain:
The http_response error was due to an outdated version of websockets (1.1.6 is now required).

The reason the digits don't change as you move the slider is because digits=input$digits is only resolved once, at the time that reactiveTable is called. In other words, the arguments you pass to reactiveTable aren't themselves magically reactive. However, you could work around this by wrapping the entire call to reactiveTable in another reactive function:

  output$mydata <- reactive(function() {

    reactiveTable(function() {

      makeData()

    }, digits=input$digits, caption="hello", caption.placement='top')()

  })

It's a little kludgy looking but will work just fine.

messages.subject: Re: Passing lists around
messages.body_plain:
A few comments on this method.

1) Is global.R documented in the tutorial?  I don't recall seeing it.

2)  Why doesn't shiny check that global.R has changed the way it checks for ui.R and server.R?

3) How does one follow this advice?

One qualification to this: when a browser reload occurs Shiny explicitly checks the timestamps of the ui.R and server.R files to see if they need to be re-sourced. If you have other scripts or data files that change Shiny isn’t aware of those, so a full stop and restart of the application is necessary to see those changes reflected.

If I am deploying a shiny app on the beta server, how do I get things to update when global.R changes?  In other words, how do I do a full stop if I'm not using runApp()?

---rjp

> Hi Randall,
>
> I think the best thing would be to have some objects in your global namespace that define the characteristics of normal, beta, gamma, and weibull. You can define these objects in a global.R file, and it will be automatically read at app startup and those objects will be visible in ui.R and server.R.
>
> Here's a gist in case the code I paste below gets mangled:
> https://gist.github.com/4136824
>
>
> # global.R
>
>
> dists <- list(
>
>
>   normal = list(
>
>
>     label = "Normal",
>
>
>     func = rnorm,
>
>
>     inputs = tagList(
>
>
>       sliderInput("mean", "mean: ", min=0, max=400, value=0),
>
>
>       sliderInput("sd", "st. dev.: ", min=0.1, max=20, value=1, step=.1)
>
>
>     ),
>
>
>     params = c("mean", "sd")
>
>
>   ),
>
>
>   beta = list(
>
>
>     label = "Beta",
>
>
>     func = rbeta,
>
>
>     inputs = tagList(
>
>
>       sliderInput("shape1", "shape1: ", min=0.1, max=10, value=1, step=0.05),
>
>
>       sliderInput("shape2", "shape2: ", min=0.1, max=10, value=1, step=0.05)
>
>
>     ),
>
>
>     params = c("shape1", "shape2")
>
>
>   )
>
>
> )
> distChoices <- names(dists)
>
>
> names(distChoices) <- sapply(dists, function(x) {x$label})
>
>
>
>
>
>
> # ui.R
>
>
> selectInput("popDist", "Population", distChoices),
>
>
> lapply(names(dists), function(name) {
>
>
>   conditionalPanel(condition = sprintf("input.popDist == '%s'", name),
>
>
>                    dists[[name]]$inputs)
>
>
> })
>
>
>
>
>
> # server.R
>
>
> params <- reactive(function() {
>
>
>   values <- lapply(dists[[input$popDist]]$params, function(param) {
>
>
>     input[param]
>
>
>   })
>
>
>   names(values) <- dists[[input$popDist]]$params
>
>
>   values
>
>
> })

>

>
>

messages.body_plain:
> 1) Is global.R documented in the tutorial?  I don't recall seeing it.

No, it was an oversight that it was left out. Hope to add it this week.

> 2)  Why doesn't shiny check that global.R has changed the way it checks for ui.R and server.R?

There's no good reason other than the way the code is factored makes implementation tricky.

> 3) How does one follow this advice?
>
> One qualification to this: when a browser reload occurs Shiny explicitly checks the timestamps of the ui.R and server.R files to see if they need to be re-sourced. If you have other scripts or data files that change Shiny isn’t aware of those, so a full stop and restart of the application is necessary to see those changes reflected.
>
> If I am deploying a shiny app on the beta server, how do I get things to update when global.R changes?  In other words, how do I do a full stop if I'm not using runApp()?

Right now there is no way to *force* a full stop, if other people are using the app. If you're the only one using the app, you can close any browsers you have pointing to it, wait 5 seconds or so, and that should cause the process to stop. Very bad, sorry.

Eventually we'll have some kind of dashboard that will let you kill/restart apps, in the meantime I'm thinking about a restart.txt mechanism like Phusion Passenger uses for Rails <http://www.modrails.com/documentation/Users%20guide%20Nginx.html#_redeploying_restarting_the_ruby_on_rails_application>.

messages.subject: Re: downloadHandler example for pdf
messages.body_plain:
Hmmm, I didn't realize there were commonly used functions in R that only took filenames. That is a bummer. I think the easiest workaround would be to write to a tempfile, then transfer the contents to the connection you're given.

output$plotpdf <- downloadHandler(
  filename = 'plot.pdf',
  content = function(con) {
    temp <- tempfile()
    on.exit(unlink(temp))
    pdf(file=temp, ...)
    ...
    dev.off()
    bytes <- readBin(temp, "raw", file.info <http://file.info>(temp)$size)
    writeBin(bytes, con)
  }
)

Does your simple implementation actually work? Oh, is the outputFile a path that's inside the www directory or something?

One advantage of using downloadHandler is that no expense is incurred unless the user actually clicks the download link; the `content` function is not invoked until the content is actually needed. This isn't the case with your reactiveUI approach, where the PDF is regenerated and pushed down to the browser every time, just in case the user does click the link.

Maybe I should revise the downloadHandler content function to take a filename instead... or, either...

I was just about to ask the same question and had a vague memory that
this was asked yesterday in the mailing list. The hack works, and I'm
using jQuery to bind the value of window.location.hash to an
input#app_hash in ui.R:

tags$head(
      tags$script("
$(document).ready(function() {
  $('#app_hash').val(window.location.hash);
});",
                  type = 'text/javascript')
    )
)

tags$input(id = 'app_url', type = 'text', style = 'display:none;')

messages.subject: Stray .RData files on glimmer.rstudio.com
messages.body_plain:
We found a bug today on the Shiny hosting service (glimmer.rstudio.com <http://glimmer.rstudio.com>) where .RData files were being created when Shiny Server asks R processes to exit prematurely (for example, when we are taking the server down to upgrade to a newer version of the software). Although usually this is harmless since ShinyApps tend not to put stuff in the global environment, I know of at least two cases where this has already caused problems.

If you'd like to purge all .RData files from your glimmer account's ShinyApps directory, please execute the following command either at an ssh prompt, or in RStudio Server under Tools | Shell.

find ~/ShinyApps -name .RData -exec rm {} +

Note that this command doesn't distinguish between .RData files that were created due to this bug, and meaningful .RData files that you put there on purpose. So if you have .RData files that matter, please rename them temporarily or something.

Sorry for the inconvenience!

messages.subject: create radiobutton list dynamically
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to create a list of radiobuttons consisting of the headers in an array selected by a drop down menu.

As you can see in this sample code - I think I need a reactive function to generate the list based on the selection. I know how  to retrieve the names of the headers, but need help with turning this into a list that can be passed to the radioButtons() on the UI side. For instance, is using reactiveText() correct?
______________________________________________
library(shiny)

# Define UI for dataset viewer application
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # Sidebar with controls to select a mineral group, with radiobutton list of minerals in that group generated in response
  sidebarPanel(
    selectInput("mineralgroup", "Choose a mineralgroup:",
                choices = c("Carbonates", "Feldspars")),

    radioButtons("min", "Mineral:",
                      ("radiolist"))

  )
))
__________________________________________________________
library(shiny)

carbonates <- read.csv("CARBONATES.csv")
feldspars <- read.csv("FELDSPARS.csv")

# Define server logic required to summarize and view the selected dataset
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  datasetInput <- reactive(function() {
    switch(input$mineralgroup,
           "Carbonates" = Carbonates,
           "Feldspars" = Feldspars)
  })
  # A reactive function creating list of radiobuttons based on "mineralgroup" choice
  output$radiolist < reactiveText(function() {
    list(names(datasetInput())
  })
})

messages.subject: Re: create radiobutton list dynamically
messages.body_plain:
I see what you're trying to do, but it won't work exactly in that way. You have two options here that I can think of.

1) Have the page contain two sets of radioButtons: one "minCarbonates" and one "minFieldspars", each one contained in its own conditionalPanel. The conditions of the conditionalPanel would be "input.mineralgroup == 'Carbonates'" and "input.mineralgroup == 'Feldspars'", respectively. If the set of radios is relatively small and well known in advance then this is likely the most robust solution. One downside is that each set of radioButtons needs its own unique inputId and in the server.R you'll need to figure out which one to use, depending on the value for mineralGroup. (So, switch(input$mineralgroup, "Carbonates"=input$minCarbonates ...) )

2) Replace radioButtons("min", "Mineral:", ("radiolist")) with uiOutput("radio"). Then in server.R, remove output$radiolist and replace with:

output$radio <- reactiveUI(function() {
  radioButtons("min", "Mineral:", names(datasetInput()))
})

This is maybe more compact and easier to understand but the reactiveUI feature is more experimental than conditionalPanel and has some edge cases (that shouldn't apply in this case though).

messages.subject: Re: downloadHandler example for pdf

Haider, FYI, I just deployed Shiny 0.2.1 which changes the content function's argument from a connection to a file path. So instead of writing your content to the connection, you now write to that file path. Thanks for the suggestion!

On Tue, Nov 27, 2012 at 6:05 PM, Haider Ali <haide...@gmail.com> wrote:

>
> Sort of tangential issue/concern that I've noticed: my plotting is wrapped in a reactive function so that it doesn't have to be called multiple times but is inside a tabPanel. However, every time you click away from the plot tab to another tab and back, it takes a noticeable amount of time to re-draw the plot (seems like it writes it to the graphics device every time). Is that the intended behavior? Is there any way to prevent this? It would make sense that everything is cached if I'm just cycling through the different tabPanels looking at different views of my data (i.e. one tab has summary stats, another has the plot, etc) and the inputs have not changed at all.
>
> Thanks
>
> -Haider
>
> On Tuesday, November 27, 2012 8:52:05 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > Hmmm, I didn't realize there were commonly used functions in R that only took filenames. That is a bummer. I think the easiest workaround would be to write to a tempfile, then transfer the contents to the connection you're given.

> > )
> >
> > Does your simple implementation actually work? Oh, is the outputFile a path that's inside the www directory or something?
> >
> > One advantage of using downloadHandler is that no expense is incurred unless the user actually clicks the download link; the `content` function is not invoked until the content is actually needed. This isn't the case with your reactiveUI approach, where the PDF is regenerated and pushed down to the browser every time, just in case the user does click the link.

I've always used the pdf function which takes a file name (not a connection) - similarly savePlot takes a file name. The example in the documentation uses write.csv which takes both file names or connections. I haven't found something similar for saving pdf files

> > > and then I just call htmlOutput('plotpdf') in the UI

> > > Is downloadHandler doing something equivalent in the background?

> > > Thanks
